title: Low-degree Kummer cohomology of a strict-local regular divisor complement
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a strictly henselian regular local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-regular-scheme], let $t\in\mathfrak m$ be a nonzerodivisor with $R/(t)$ regular, and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $R$. Put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/t]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Use small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and $A(1)=\mu_\ell$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. The restriction maps $A\to H^0(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\mu_\ell(R)\to H^0(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_\ell)$ are isomorphisms. There exists a primitive $\ell$-th root $\zeta\in R^\times$, and $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ identifies $A_S$ with $\mu_{\ell,S}$ (and hence also their restrictions to $V$). If $\kappa(t)\in H^1(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_\ell)$ is the connecting class of the unit $t$ for the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], then the $A$-linear map
$$A\longrightarrow H^1(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_\ell),\qquad a\longmapsto a\kappa(t)$$
is an isomorphism.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.2, printed p.245, low-degree input; reconstructed without the excluded reference using Stacks Tags 03PL (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-kummer-sequence), 0AFZ (more-algebra.tex, lemma-regular-local-Pic-zero), and 0AG0 (more-algebra.tex, lemma-regular-local-UFD).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] to both regular local rings $R$ and $R/(t)$. Thus $R$ is a domain and $(t)$ is a proper prime ideal. The nonzerodivisor $t$ is nonzero, and it is not a unit because $t\in\mathfrak m$. Write $B=R[1/t]$. From the fraction description of localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away], $R\to B$ is injective and $B$ is a nonzero domain: a fraction is zero only when some power of $t$ annihilates its numerator. The prime $(0)$ is a point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in every nonempty basic open. Hence any two nonempty opens meet, so $V$ is nonempty and connected.

source.place: Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain; elementary fraction and prime-spectrum consequences

proof.text: Every $v\in B^\times$ has a unique expression $v=ut^m$ with $u\in R^\times$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. Indeed write $v=x/t^a$ and $v^{-1}=y/t^b$ with $a,b\geq0$. Injectivity of $R\to B$ gives $xy=t^{a+b}$ in $R$. Prove by induction on $N$ that $xy=t^N$ implies $x=u t^c$ for a unit $u$ and $0\leq c\leq N$. For $N=0$, $xy=1$. For $N>0$, primality of $(t)$ implies $x=tx'$ or $y=ty'$; cancel the nonzero $t$ and apply induction to $x'y=t^{N-1}$ or $xy'=t^{N-1}$. This gives the required expression with $m=c-a$. For uniqueness, $ut^m=u't^{m'}$ with $m>m'$ would imply $u'=ut^{m-m'}\in(t)$, contradicting that $u'$ is a unit; reverse the roles if $m'<m$ is replaced by $m'>m$. Equality of exponents then gives $u=u'$. Conversely every $ut^m$ is invertible. Multiplication adds exponents, so $B^\times\cong R^\times\times\mathbf Z$ by $(u,m)\mapsto ut^m$.

source.place: Elementary prime-divisor calculation underlying Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD; only primality from Step 1 is needed

proof.text: The group $R^\times$ is $\ell$-divisible. For $u\in R^\times$, reduce $f(X)=X^\ell-u$ modulo $\mathfrak m$. Its derivative is $\ell X^{\ell-1}$, which is nonzero at any root, since $\ell$ and $u$ remain nonzero in the residue field $k$. Thus $\overline f$ is separable. As $k$ is separably closed, an irreducible factor of this separable polynomial is linear, giving a nonzero root $a_0\in k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] to this monic $f$ and its simple root $a_0$. The lift $a\in R$ has $a^\ell=u$ and is a unit (its inverse is $a^{\ell-1}u^{-1}$).

source.place: Tags 04GF, definition-henselian, and 04GG, lemma-characterize-henselian; application to X^ell-u

proof.text: By [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity], $\mu_\ell(R)$ is cyclic of order $\ell$; choose a generator $\zeta$. Its powers $\zeta^a$ ($0\leq a<\ell$) have pairwise unit differences, since $\zeta^a-\zeta^b=\zeta^b(\zeta^{a-b}-1)$. Successive division by the monic linear factors gives $X^\ell-1=\prod_{a=0}^{\ell-1}(X-\zeta^a)$: after dividing out any factors, evaluation at the next root and cancellation of the preceding unit differences gives remainder zero; degrees and leading coefficients finish. For any etale $U\to S$ and $y\in\mu_\ell(U)$ as in [def-asd-etale-roots-of-unity], the opens $U_a$ on which all $y-\zeta^b$ for $b\neq a$ are units cover $U$. At a point the residue field makes the displayed product zero, and pairwise unit differences allow exactly one vanishing factor. On $U_a$ the product identity forces $y=\zeta^a$. These opens are disjoint. Thus $y$ is uniquely a locally constant choice of $a\in\mathbf F_\ell$. Conversely such choices glue to a root. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] this proves $A_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell,S}$, $a\mapsto\zeta^a$, on every test object. Multiplication of roots is addition of exponents, so it is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. The same construction on test schemes over $V$ gives its restriction there.

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps; Section 03PK, section-kummer; elementary factorization with the roots supplied by the cited node

proof.text: Since $V$ is nonempty and connected (Step 1), any locally constant map $V\to A$ is constant: the inverse image of a value is both open and closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] and the degree-zero definition in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], the restriction $A\to H^0(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ is an isomorphism. The isomorphism of Step 4 identifies $\mu_\ell(R)$ with $A$ and $H^0(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_\ell)$ with $H^0(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, with restriction sending $\zeta^a$ to the constant section $\zeta^a$. This proves the second claimed restriction isomorphism as well.

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps; degree zero of cohomology

proof.text: We next prove that every invertible $\mathcal O_V$-module $\mathcal L$ is trivial. Such a module is quasi-coherent and locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. Set $P=\Gamma(V,\mathcal L)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], $\widetilde P\cong\mathcal L$. Refine its local trivializations to basic opens $D(f_i)$. A finite subcover exists by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; its $f_i$ generate the unit ideal, because otherwise a maximal ideal containing all of them would give an uncovered point. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], $P_{f_i}=\mathcal L(D(f_i))\cong B_{f_i}$. The criterion [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-projective] therefore makes $P$ finite projective. At each prime of $B$, one of these $f_i$ is invertible, so further localization gives $P_{\mathfrak q}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$ of rank one. Now [lem-trf-regular-local-pic-zero], with $A=R$ and $f=t$, gives $P\cong B$. Applying tilde and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] (rank one) yields $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_V$. This verifies the scheme-theoretic Picard vanishing from the algebraic statement, without assuming that $B$ is local or semilocal.

source.place: Tag 0AFZ, lemma-regular-local-Pic-zero; Schemes Tags 01HV and 01IA; Algebra Tags 00NX and 00E8 for the affine dictionary

proof.text: Apply the scheme version [thm-sc-hilbert-90] to $V$: Step 6 makes its group of invertible modules zero, so $H^1(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf G_m)=0$. Since $\ell$ is invertible in $B$, [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] gives the short exact sequence $1\to\mu_\ell\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{(-)^\ell}\mathbf G_m\to1$ on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder], taking its scheme map to be $\mathrm{id}_V$. The resulting exact segment is $B^\times\xrightarrow{(-)^\ell} B^\times\xrightarrow{\delta} H^1(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_\ell)\to0$. Hence $\delta$ induces an isomorphism $B^\times/(B^\times)^\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_\ell)$, and by definition $\delta(t)=\kappa(t)$.

source.place: Tag 03P8, theorem-picard-group; Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence and the displayed long exact sequence immediately following it

proof.text: Under the decomposition of Step 2, the $\ell$-power map sends $(u,m)$ to $(u^\ell,\ell m)$. Step 3 makes its image precisely $R^\times\times\ell\mathbf Z$. Therefore the exponent modulo $\ell$ induces an isomorphism $B^\times/(B^\times)^\ell\cong\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z=A$ whose inverse sends $\overline m$ to $[t^m]$. Composing this inverse with Step 7 gives $\overline m\mapsto\delta(t^m)=m\delta(t)=m\kappa(t)$. An additive homomorphism between groups killed by $\ell$ commutes with multiplication by integers modulo $\ell$, so this is an $A$-linear isomorphism. It is exactly the map in the statement, with the generator and sign fixed by the Kummer connecting morphism.

split_report.summary: Kept the complete statement and all inherited searches. Reconstructed the low-degree Kummer computation in eight steps using existing DAG nodes only. Proved the localized-unit normal form directly from the prime ideal (t), avoiding unnecessary factoriality, proved the roots-of-unity sheaf trivialization on test schemes, and supplied the affine-module/Picard comparison and exact-sequence argument. No new nodes, no Lean edits or builds.

Steps 1-5 realize the degree-zero and coefficient trivialization input, Steps 6-8 the Kummer generator in degree one; no chapter or unit route is changed.

tool_uses.why: Simple-root lifting proves divisibility of units; no perverse-unit lemma supplies this henselian algebra tool.
The cyclic group and unit-difference statements supply a primitive root and its sheaf trivialization; used solely as local algebra.
The ordinary constant-sheaf section formula identifies the root sheaf and degree-zero restriction; no perverse-unit lemma gives this general site tool.
The finite basic-open freeness criterion makes the sections of a line bundle finite projective, needed to apply the existing Picard lemma.
This generic algebra theorem trivializes rank-one modules over R[1/t]; no trace-formula proof route is imported.
The general-scheme Picard/H1 identification applies to V of arbitrary dimension; the curve-only h1-gm-pic node does not.
The Kummer short exact sequence on any scheme applies to V; it does not use any purity route.
Clause 2, specialized to id_V, supplies the ordinary etale cohomology long exact sequence; no base-change result is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NG-ba8890eca (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's 8 steps and the statement of every cited node in full. No new nodes and no fixes. Source: ILO XVI Prop 3.4.2 (printed p.245, PDF p.251) only says the criterion follows from the q in {0,1} calculation and defers that calculation to SGA 4½ Cycle 2.1.4. The delivery rebuilds it without SGA from Stacks 00NP, 04GG, 03P5, 03P8, 03PL and 0AFZ; I checked each tag exists in literature/stacks-project, and proof_origin is marked agent. Step 1: R/(t) regular local gives a domain, so (t) is prime, R injects into B = R[1/t], B is a domain and V is connected. Step 2: I checked the induction on xy = t^N and the uniqueness argument, which give B^× = R^× × t^Z. Step 3: X^ℓ − u is separable over the separably closed residue field and lifts by henselian root lifting, so R^× is ℓ-divisible. Step 4: roots of unity form a cyclic group with unit differences; the open sets U_a are disjoint and cover, which gives A_S ≅ μ_ℓ through constant-sheaf sections. Step 5: H^0 equals global sections and V is connected. Step 6: L ≅ P~, a finite basic-open cover with 00NX makes P finite projective of rank 1, then 0AFZ with A = R, f = t gives P ≅ B; every hypothesis is checked. Step 7: Hilbert 90 (any scheme) gives H^1(G_m) = 0, and the Kummer sequence with clause 2 of the long exact ladder at id_V gives B^×/ℓ ≅ H^1(μ_ℓ). Step 8: B^×/ℓ ≅ Z/ℓ, and m maps to mκ(t), A-linear. Small cases: dim 0 is excluded since t ≠ 0; dim 1 gives the strictly henselian DVR, K^×/ℓ = Z/ℓ; t = xy shows the R/(t)-regular hypothesis is needed; ℓ = 2 is fine. Duplicate search over the DAG (Kummer, Pic, 0AFZ, strict-local nodes in sbc and per) found nothing that states this calculation. Batch-5 flag on lem-trf-regular-local-pic-zero: accepted. It is Stacks 0AFZ, pure commutative algebra that neither assumption gives, so it cannot be replaced by an assumption leaf. Its own closure reaches only generic K_0 and determinant trf nodes and no trace-formula or duality theorem; it sits in sec-trace-formula only because of the UFD boundary factorization there. The 8 tool_uses are accepted as generic tools.
